title: Anti-Reflection Coated Thin Chromium
scientific_hypothesis: A thin Cr layer with an HfO2/SiO2 anti-reflection coating at the air interface will minimize visible reflection while the aluminum substrate provides near-infrared reflection, achieving high visible absorptance with minimal Cr thickness.
design_principle: Anti-reflection coatings reduce surface reflection through destructive interference of reflected waves. By applying an AR coating to thin Cr, visible reflection is minimized allowing more light to enter and be absorbed by Cr. The Al substrate naturally reflects IR. L02 supports triple-layer dielectric designs for optical loss reduction.
proposed_topology: Air / SiO2 / HfO2 / Cr / SiO2 / Al substrate
soft_objectives: Minimize reflectance in 400-700 nm through AR coating
Maximize absorptance in 400-700 nm through Cr
Maximize reflectance in 700-2000 nm through Al substrate
manufacturing_considerations: Total 5 layers including Cr and dielectric + Al substrate
AR coating requires precise thickness for target wavelength
L02 supports triple-layer approach for loss reduction
theory_basis: Thin film interference for reflection minimization
expected_advantages: Low material cost with thin Cr
known_risks: AR coating bandwidth may be limited
Thin Cr may not absorb all visible light
IR reflectance depends heavily on Al substrate quality
execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer stack with air incidence on an aluminum substrate. Stack sequence from air to substrate: SiO2 (Lemarchand) / HfO2 / Cr (Rakic-LD) / SiO2 (Lemarchand), terminating at aluminum substrate. Total layer count is 5 (2 SiO2 (Lemarchand) + 1 HfO2 + 1 Cr (Rakic-LD) + Al (Rakic-LD) substrate not counted as film layer). Optimize the thickness of each layer independently to create an anti-reflection effect at the air interface. Wavelength range 400-2000 nm. Target: minimize reflectance and maximize absorptance in 400-700 nm, maximize reflectance in 700-2000 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light.
